ic_name: DALI (Digital Addressable Lighting Interface, IEC 62386 via TI SLAA422A)
initialization_sequence_control_gear: 1. Power-up reset. Hardware brown-out / power-on reset.
2. TI_DALI_Init(FWKEY): configure DALI_RX (P2.0) as edge-interrupt input; configure DALI_TX (P2.1), TPS62260_ENABLE (P1.0/F2131 or P1.1/G2xx2), PWM1, PWM2 as outputs.

3. Copy persistent variables from information-memory flash into RAM (Power On Level, Min/Max, Fade Rate/Time, Short Address, Group bitmaps, Scene 0..15, Random Address, Fast Fade Time, Failure Status, Operating Mode, Dimming Curve).
4. Configure WDT+ interval mode: WDT_MDLY_8 (SMCLK/8192) ≈ 1 ms tick — drives fade timing and special-command timeouts.

5. Configure Timer_A3 PWM: TACTL = TASSEL_2+ID_0+MC_0+TACLR (SMCLK = 8 MHz); TACCR0 = 5000 (PWM period 5000 counts → 1.6 kHz); TACCR1 = LED[power_on_level]; TACCR2 = LED[power_on_level]; TACCTL1 = CM_0+CCIS_2+OUTMOD_3; TACCTL2 = CM_0+CCIS_2+OUTMOD_3 (set on TACCRx, reset on TACCR0).
6. P1OUT &= ~BIT0  (turn off LEDs); TACTL |= MC_1 (start Timer_A in up mode).
8. TI_DALI_Transaction_Loop() — enter the forever-loop that polls DALI_RX, decodes Manchester forward frames, dispatches commands, schedules backward frames and fade tasks. Should never return.
9. Within 600 ms after power-up, if no DALI command arrives, the device automatically applies the Power On Level.
typical_forward_frame_reception_sequence: 1. DALI bus idle (HIGH). DALI_RX_PxIE armed for edge.
2. Start-bit edge fires Port-2 ISR; CPU captures timestamp and re-arms for mid-bit boundary.
3. CPU Manchester-decodes 16 information bits (address byte + data byte, MSB first) over ≈ 13.3 ms (16 × 833 μs).
4. CPU verifies 2 stop bits (line HIGH for ≥ 2 × bit-time).
5. Address match: short / group / broadcast / special-command pattern against this gear's Short Address / Group bitmap / Configuration-Mode flag.
6. On mismatch → silently return to step 2 after settling.
7. On match → decode B bit. B=0: Target Level := Data byte (special-case 255 = MASK, 0 = OFF). B=1: dispatch on command code.
8. If indirect command launches a fade, set Fade Target = Target Level, enable WDT+ fade-tick contributions; if instantaneous (DAPC / OFF / RESET / RECALL MAX/MIN) apply immediately.
9. If query → set flag to send backward frame after 7×TE settle.
10. Wait ≥ 22×TE before re-arming for next forward frame.
typical_backward_frame_transmission_sequ: 1. Backward-frame pending flag set by query handler.
2. Wait until 7×TE (≈ 2.92 ms) after end of forward frame.
3. Drive DALI_TX LOW for half-bit (Manchester '1' start bit).
4. Shift out 8 data bits MSB-first, Manchester-encoded at 1200 baud (≈ 6.67 ms).
5. Release line HIGH for 2 stop bits (≈ 1.67 ms).
6. Re-arm DALI_RX edge interrupt; clear backward-frame pending flag.
configuration_mode_addressing_iteration: 1. Control device broadcasts INITIALIZE (0xA5, data byte 0x00) → all gear enter Configuration Mode for 15 minutes.
2. Control device broadcasts RANDOMIZE (0xA7) → each gear generates a fresh 24-bit Random Address.
3. Control device performs bisection: SEARCH ADDRESS H/M/L (0xB1/0xB3/0xB5) load Search Address := 0xFFFFFF.
4. Control device sends COMPARE (0xA9) → every gear whose Random Address ≤ Search Address answers 0xFF.
5. If multiple gear answer, control device halves the Search Address window and repeats COMPARE until exactly one gear answers.
6. Control device sends QUERY SHORT ADDRESS (0xBB) → the matching gear answers its currently stored Short Address (or 0xFF if unassigned).
7. Control device loads DTR := new short address (special command DTR 0xA3); then PROGRAM SHORT ADDRESS (0xB7) → matching gear writes DTR into its Short Address persistent variable.
8. Control device sends VERIFY SHORT ADDRESS (0xB9, data = new candidate) → verifying gear answers 0xFF.
9. Control device sends WITHDRAW (0xAB) → matching gear drops out; iterate from step 3 until all gear addressed.
10. Control device sends TERMINATE (0xA1) → all gear exit Configuration Mode.
scene_recall_sequence: 1. Pre-programmed: Control device sets DTR := desired scene level, then sends STORE DTR AS SCENE n (0x40..0x4F) to each gear (broadcast or short-addressed).
2. Recall: Control device sends GO TO SCENE n (0x10..0x1F).
3. Each gear retrieves Scene[n] from non-volatile storage; if Scene[n] == 0xFF (MASK), command is ignored.
4. Otherwise Actual Level fades to Scene[n] at the configured Fade Time.
group_addressing_sequence: 1. Pre-programmed: Control device sends ADD TO GROUP n (0x60..0x6F) to each gear (short address) to set the group-membership bit.
2. Recall: Control device sends a forward frame with Y=1, AAAA = n in the upper 4 bits, lower 2 bits = 00.
3. All gear whose group bitmap bit n = 1 receive and execute the command.
broadcast_sequence: 1. Control device sends forward frame with address byte 0xFE (Y=1, AAAAAA=111111, B=0) for direct level or 0xFF (B=1) for indirect command.
2. Every gear on the bus receives.
3. Each addressed gear executes; no backward frame (queries shall not be broadcast — collision risk).
two_strike_commit_sequence: 1. Control device sends destructive command (RESET, STORE DTR AS SHORT ADDRESS, STORE DTR AS SCENE n, STORE DTR AS MAX/MIN/SYSTEM_FAILURE/POWER_ON_LEVEL/FADE TIME/FADE RATE).
2. Gear records the command in a one-deep pending buffer; does NOT yet commit.
3. Within 100 ms control device sends the identical command again.
5. If only one delivery arrives within 100 ms, the pending command is discarded.
fade_sequence: 1. Forward frame requests a new Target Level (direct or via RECALL/SCENE).
2. Fade engine computes step size: (Target - Actual) / (steps_in_FadeTime).
3. WDT+ interval ISR (≈ 1 ms tick) increments / decrements Actual Level by the step size each tick.
4. TI_DALI_Update_Callback() sets TACCTL1 |= CCIE so Timer_A1 ISR refreshes TACCR1/TACCR2 from LED[actual_level] on the next PWM cycle; ISR then clears CCIE to disable itself.
5. When Actual Level == Target Level, fade-running status bit is cleared.
power_fail_flash_update_sequence: 1. Comparator_A+ (or external trigger) signals VCC about to drop below 2.2 V.
3. Two information-memory segments are erased (4.5 ms each).
4. 32 byte-writes at 333 kHz × 30 cycles per byte ≈ 2.88 ms total programming time.
5. Cumulative update fits within the MSP430F2xx 10 ms maximum.
6. Hardware must hold VCC ≥ 2.2 V for ≥ 3 ms during this window.
interrupt_handling_sequence_TI: 1. Port-2 ISR (DALI_RX edge) — captures Manchester bit edges; updates the bit-reception state machine.
2. WDT+ ISR — increments idle_time global (1 ms per tick); drives fade timing and special-command timeouts.
3. TIMERA1_VECTOR ISR — fires only when TI_DALI_Update_Callback enables CCIE; updates TACCR1 / TACCR2 from LED[actual_level]; disables CCIE again before returning.
unsupported_command_handling_sequence: 1. Forward frame received with command 129 (Enable Write Memory) or 275 (WRITE MEMORY LOCATION 0xC7) or 224..227 (RSP/CP/SDC).
2. Gear decodes address but command-dispatch table returns 'unsupported'.
3. Gear silently discards the frame — no backward frame, no error indication.
4. If the unsupported command was a query in 242..251 range, command 240 (QUERY EXTENDED VERSION NUMBER family) shall indicate this feature is not implemented.
